name: Baśka
description: Baśka (pronounced 'Bash-ka') is a distinctively fast-paced, 16-card trick-taking game from the Kashubian region of northern Poland. A member of the Schafkopf family, it is played with just the highest honors from a standard deck (A, 10, Q, J). The game is celebrated for its secret partnerships determined by the possession of 'Old Ones' (Black Queens) and its high-stakes solo bids.
deck: 16 cards (Standard deck ranks A, 10, Q, J)

history.origins: Developed in the Kashubian communities along the Baltic Sea. It is an adaptation of the German game 'Kop' (Head), which itself is a simplified version of Schafkopf. The name 'Baśka' is a Kashubian diminutive for 'Barbara'.
timeline: 1800s: High-honor variants of Schafkopf appear in Northern Europe.
Early 1900s: Baśka becomes the dominant card game in the Kashubian region of Poland.
1990s: Formalization of rules for regional tournaments in Poland.
Present: Recognized as a cultural mascot of the Kashubian people, with numerous local clubs and championships.
history.cultural: Commonly played in traditional Kashubian 'karczma' (taverns). Knowing how to bid 'Gran' or 'Zolo' is a mark of local prestige.
history.evolution: The simplification down to 16 cards (from the traditional 32 or 24) makes the game exceptionally aggressive and requires perfect memory of all cards in play.

setup.players: 4 players. Two are 'The Old Ones' (holders of Black Queens) and two are the opponents.
setup.deck: 16 cards: Ace, 10, Queen, and Jack of each suit.
setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 4 cards (usually 2 and 2).
setup.equipment: 16-card specific pack or a stripped 52-card deck (keep A, 10, Q, J only).

rules.objective: The 'Old Ones' must capture a majority of the 104 available points in the round (or win all tricks in solo bids).
rules.gameplay: Players must follow suit. Trumps count as their own suit (The 'Trump' suit). If a trump is led, all others MUST play trumps. If an off-suit (e.g., Ace of Spades) is led, players must follow Spades.
keyRules: Point Values: Ace (11), 10 (10), Queen (3), Jack (2). Total = 104 points.
Winning: The declarer/partnership needs 53 points (104 / 2 + 1) to win.
Contra: Opponents can shout 'Kontra' to double the points for the round if they believe they can beat the bid.

strategy.basic: Identify your partner immediately. If you hold a Black Queen, watch who plays the other one.
strategy.intermediate: Counting the 16: You absolute MUST remember all 16 cards. If you see two Aces of off-suits played, you know the remaining two are high-risk targets for trumping.
strategy.advanced: The Gran Lead: In a Gran bid, where only Jacks are trump, high-ranking suits (Aces and Tens) become much more powerful. Lead your strongest suit to flush out the opponents' Jacks.
tips: Don't bid 'Zolo' unless you hold at least two Queens OR the QC and another high trump.
In standard play, the Ace of Hearts is the 9th highest trump. Don't be fooled into thinking it's a weak card.

variations.name: Bez Atu
variations.description: A variation where only Aces and Tens are points, and no trumps exist (very rare).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Bez Atu is documented here but not yet modeled as a separate engine ruleset; the base Baśka engine describes the standard trump game.

variations.name: Silent Zolo
variations.description: A player plays solo without announcing it until the first trick is played.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Silent Zolo is a bidding and scoring twist on top of the base Baśka rules and is not represented with explicit engine overrides yet.

scoring.description: Scoring is zero-sum based on the contract value.

synthesis.shortDescription: Experience the lightning-fast 16-card classic from Poland. Identify your secret partner, master the Queens and Jacks, and go solo in the high-stakes 'Gran' and 'Zolo' bids. 4 cards, 4 tricks, infinite strategy.
